title: A Contribution to Our Knowledge of Rivea Corymbosa: The Narcotic Ololiuqui of the Aztecs
shortTitle: A Contribution to Our Knowledge of Rivea Corymbosa
author: Richard Evans Schultes
summary: Schultes's botanical monograph settling the identity of ololiuqui, the Aztec morning-glory narcotic. He credits Urbina's 1897 identification as Rivea corymbosa, corrects Safford's 1915 misidentification as jimsonweed, and surveys continued ritual and medicinal use among the Chinantec, Mazatec, Mixtec, and Zapotec of Oaxaca.
excerpt: "In 1897, Urbina correctly identified ololiuqui as Rivea corymbosa (L.) Hall. f., but, in 1915, Safford referred ololiuqui to Datura meteloides... The Safford identification, although erroneous, gained wide acceptance, and, in spite of a reaffirmation of the Urbina identification by Reko in 1934, has persisted."
citation: Schultes, Richard Evans. A Contribution to Our Knowledge of Rivea Corymbosa: The Narcotic Ololiuqui of the Aztecs. Cambridge, Mass.: Botanical Museum of Harvard University, 1941.

draft.rationale: The definitive early-twentieth-century botanical identification of ololiuqui, closing a debate that had run since Safford's 1915 misidentification. This is the companion piece to Schultes's 1940 mushroom paper and the direct scholarly ancestor of Hofmann's 1960 isolation of ergot alkaloids from the same plant.
